findings.evidenceJa: ずるり、と滑る腕で地面を掴み
findings.governingReading: He grips the ground with his arm slipping slickly beneath him.
findings.explanation: The English omits the unstable sliding of the only limb supporting his nearly severed body.

findings.evidenceJa: かすかな心臓の鼓動
findings.governingReading: the faint beat of his heart
findings.explanation: The English removes the faintness that marks Shirou as barely alive.

findings.evidenceJa: ギチギチと音をたてる、傷ついた内臓
findings.governingReading: his damaged internal organs making a tight creaking or grinding sound
findings.explanation: The English invents personified pain and omits that the injured organs produce the same mechanical sound later associated with internal blades.

findings.evidenceJa: 鉄でも入っているのか
findings.governingReading: Is there iron inside his arm or body?
findings.explanation: mirror moon again generalizes explicit iron into unspecified metal.

findings.highlight: With a creaking noise, my body reacts
findings.evidenceJa: 体は鈍い音をたてながら
findings.governingReading: His body answers his will while making a dull, heavy sound.
findings.explanation: Creaking supplies a different acoustic quality from the source’s muffled, dull impact-like noise.

findings.highlight: the things I need to live flow out
findings.evidenceJa: 生きていくのに必要なものがごっそりとこぼれ落ちていく
findings.governingReading: something necessary for life spills out of the wound in a great mass each time he strains
findings.explanation: The English loses the wholesale quantity and changes spilling from a wound into neutral flowing.

findings.evidenceJa: もう無理だ
findings.governingReading: his body cannot continue; it is already impossible
findings.explanation: Useless evaluates purpose or utility, while Saber is pleading that further bodily effort is impossible.

findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの声は、罵倒に近かった
findings.governingReading: Saber’s tone comes close to a verbal denunciation or shouted abuse.
findings.explanation: Insulting can describe offensive content; the source marks how forcefully her voice has broken from formal restraint.

findings.evidenceJa: 俺のあがきを嘲笑っているギルガメッシュ
findings.governingReading: Gilgamesh, who is laughing Shirou’s desperate struggle to scorn
findings.explanation: The English lists Gilgamesh as an obstacle but removes his active mockery of Shirou’s effort.

findings.evidenceJa: この心が折れて、しまう
findings.governingReading: his heart or resolve will break
findings.explanation: Mind will die is nonidiomatic and turns emotional collapse into cognitive death.

findings.evidenceJa: こんな事で貴方に死なれたら
findings.governingReading: If Shirou dies over something like this or for this cause
findings.explanation: Here converts Saber’s anguished judgment of cause and worth into physical location.

findings.highlight: How can she say such selfish things
findings.evidenceJa: よくも言いたい放題
findings.governingReading: How dare she say whatever she pleases without understanding his feelings
findings.explanation: Selfish supplies a moral judgment absent from Shirou’s frustrated complaint and loses the uncontrolled torrent of speech.

findings.evidenceJa: 独りよがりの幸せ
findings.governingReading: self-satisfied happiness defined by one side alone
findings.explanation: Complacent describes passivity or overconfidence; Shirou is criticizing a unilateral conception of another person’s happiness.

findings.highlight: So that you can be proud of your life
findings.evidenceJa: 胸を張って眠れるように
findings.governingReading: so that at death Saber can hold her head high and go to sleep, proud of her life
findings.explanation: The English retains pride but omits sleep, the merciful completion of Shirou’s wish for Saber’s final rest.

findings.evidenceJa: 口にしたかった
findings.governingReading: He wanted to put the feeling into words.
findings.explanation: Had to makes external or moral necessity replace Shirou’s personal desire to speak in this unclouded moment.

findings.highlight: My magical energy is my life.
findings.evidenceJa: 魔力とは、すなわち命だ
findings.governingReading: Magical power is, in other words, life itself.
findings.explanation: Adding possessives turns Shirou’s categorical equivalence into a merely personal resource statement.

findings.highlight: I can’t give Saber to you.
findings.evidenceJa: おまえに、セイバーは任せられない
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot entrust Saber to Gilgamesh.
findings.explanation: Give Saber to you repeats the ownership framing Shirou has just rejected; 任せる concerns trust and care, not transfer of property.

findings.highlight: the light that can burn away everything it touches
findings.evidenceJa: 触れるモノを焼き払う光の渦
findings.governingReading: a vortex of light that burns away whatever it touches
findings.explanation: The English omits the vortex form of the attack that stops Shirou’s projection.

findings.evidenceJa: シロウ、それを
findings.governingReading: “Shirou, that—!”
findings.explanation: The English invents “let me” as the completion of Saber’s interrupted words, advancing an unspecified exclamation into a request.

findings.evidenceJa: 傍らには寄り添ったセイバーの姿
findings.governingReading: Beside him is Saber’s figure pressed close against him.
findings.explanation: The English preserves position but omits her physically drawing close after taking his hand.

findings.evidenceJa: ギルガメッシュの剣
findings.governingReading: Gilgamesh’s sword, read specifically as Gram
findings.explanation: The English drops the Gram ruby and therefore the weapon identity Shirou associates with the repelled attack.

findings.highlight: needs to kill everything he sees in order to calm down
findings.evidenceJa: 殺さねば気が済まぬ
findings.governingReading: will not be satisfied until everything in sight is dead
findings.explanation: Calm down turns murderous satisfaction into emotional regulation and psychologizes the rage differently.

findings.evidenceJa: 緊張の糸が切れて
findings.governingReading: the taut thread of tension snaps
findings.explanation: The English removes the thread-breaking image that causes Shirou’s body to collapse.

findings.evidenceJa: 尻餅をついた状態で、セイバーに背中を支えられながら
findings.governingReading: Seated heavily on the ground, Shirou looks down while Saber supports his back.
findings.explanation: The English omits both his seated fall and the exact support at his back, weakening spatial continuity into the later embrace.

findings.highlight: My body, cut from my left shoulder, should have died instantly.
findings.evidenceJa: 体は、本来なら即死の傷だ
findings.governingReading: The diagonal wound through his body would ordinarily cause instant death.
findings.explanation: The English makes the body itself the subject that “should have died,” producing malformed physiology and obscuring the wound’s lethality.

findings.evidenceJa: 無数の剣
findings.governingReading: countless swords
findings.explanation: Many reduces the apparently innumerable blades crowding inside and reconnecting Shirou’s body.

findings.highlight: It must have been my imagination
findings.evidenceJa: さっきのは幻か
findings.governingReading: Was what he just saw an illusion?
findings.explanation: The English promotes Shirou’s question into a definite dismissal, despite the immediate restoration and later sheath recognition.

findings.evidenceJa: それは、どのくらいの強さだったのか
findings.governingReading: How strong was that embrace or pressure?
findings.explanation: The English turns Shirou’s fading perception of the embrace’s strength into a general question about Saber’s power.

findings.evidenceJa: 深く染みいるような声
findings.governingReading: a voice that seems to soak deeply into him
findings.explanation: Seeping voice is unnatural and can suggest liquid leakage rather than words penetrating Shirou emotionally.

findings.evidenceJa: 眠りに身を委ねる
findings.governingReading: He entrusts or yields himself to sleep.
findings.explanation: The English splits body from self and makes sleep a controlled bodily permission rather than surrender of consciousness.

findings.highlight: it would have been more perfect if our positions were reversed
findings.evidenceJa: この立場が逆だったら文句はない
findings.governingReading: He lets slip the petty complaint that he would have no objection if their positions were reversed.
findings.explanation: More perfect adds an evaluative ideal absent from the comic complaint and smooths its bluntness.
